title: Order and evidence transfer in EAL/2 model sequences
question: On six exposed EAL/2 regression tasks, how do endpoint correctness, unsupported positive answers and total cost differ by model sequence, tool placement and transferred record?

scope.system_or_population: Six engineering-v2.1-eal2 synthetic tasks and six pinned OpenAI model snapshots
scope.conditions: 27 frozen one-, two- and three-stage conditions; fixed source/observations/time and fresh host sessions; low reasoning effort for GPT-5 family
scope.spatial_scope: Local EAL host with authorised remote OpenAI generation; no physical apparatus
scope.temporal_scope: One campaign after protocol and implementation freeze, two repetitions per task-condition
exclusions: Independent evidence from repeated model agreement

claims.statement: Transferring tool evidence from full GPT-4.1 to GPT-4.1 nano improves endpoint correctness relative to transferring its answer alone on this task suite.
claims.scope_limit: Finite exposed synthetic suite and specified snapshots; pilot estimation only
claims.success_consequence: Retain this transfer scheme for a new independent task study
claims.failure_consequence: Revise the transfer representation or retain simpler answering

assumptions.statement: Task reference labels correspond to the documented EAL semantics and remain fixed across arms.
assumptions.test_or_justification: Known-answer checks, original analytic oracles and adversarial scorer tests; all references must pass before requests
assumptions.failure_consequence: Suspend affected accuracy comparisons and retain raw outcomes

assumptions.statement: Provider snapshot behaviour is sufficiently stable during the campaign for a contemporaneous finite-task contrast.
assumptions.test_or_justification: Randomised rotating order, response model IDs and fingerprints retained; no claim of sampling determinism
assumptions.failure_consequence: Report stratified descriptive records and repeat after stability is restored

assumptions.statement: No scoring information enters stage prompts or hand-offs.
assumptions.test_or_justification: Allow-listed packets, canary leak tests, isolated fresh hosts and no outcome-based routing
assumptions.failure_consequence: Invalidate affected model results and repair under a new freeze

hypotheses.label: Evidence transfer benefit
hypotheses.statement: Grounded tool records let the smaller recipient correct misleading or insufficient producer answers, increasing endpoint correctness.
hypotheses.scope: Only the frozen finite suite, snapshots and prompt budgets

hypotheses.label: Additional evidence ineffective
hypotheses.statement: The recipient copies the producer conclusion or misreads additional evidence; answer-only transfer performs at least as well.
hypotheses.scope: Only the frozen finite suite, snapshots and prompt budgets

hypotheses.label: Budget and repetition rival
hypotheses.statement: Apparent sequence gains arise from extra model calls or a stronger final model rather than transferred evidence.
hypotheses.scope: Only the frozen finite suite, snapshots and prompt budgets

hypotheses.label: Primary null
hypotheses.statement: H_0: Delta_EA <= 0, where Delta_EA = mean_task mean_repeat(Y_evidence - Y_answer).
hypotheses.scope: Only the frozen finite suite, snapshots and prompt budgets

hypotheses.label: Primary alternative
hypotheses.statement: H_1: Delta_EA > 0. A practically relevant pilot difference is at least 0.10; no confirmatory significance claim is planned.
hypotheses.scope: Only the frozen finite suite, snapshots and prompt budgets

predictions.expected_pattern: For identical producer outputs, evidence yields more correct recipient endpoints than answer-only transfer.
predictions.tolerance: Exact status equality; descriptive task-cluster interval

predictions.expected_pattern: Evidence performs no better than answer-only transfer despite equal producer records and equal recipient stage thresholds.

design.rationale: Matched producer output makes the evidence-versus-answer contrast interpretable; crossovers and same-model chains expose order and repetition effects.

design.assignment_method: Seeded rotating condition order; shared prefixes within each task/repetition, provider sampling unseeded
design.masking: Scorer is deterministic; models blind to outcome labels
design.comparator: Primary l_tool_n_evidence minus l_tool_n_answer; secondary reversed and homogeneous sequences and solo endpoints

identification.causal_and_measurement_structure: Task and repeat -> shared producer; hand-off condition -> recipient prompt -> endpoint. Producer output is fixed across the primary contrast; final model and stage limits are equal.
identified_parameters: Finite-sample paired difference in common endpoint correctness
threats: Evidence prompt length is part of treatment
diagnostics: Model IDs, failure classes and prompt token counts
rescue_actions: Report incomplete or unstable contrasts as descriptive only
New independent tasks and separate token-matched study

sampling.method: Fixed purposive feasibility suite; no outcome-dependent sample expansion
sampling.sample_size_or_information_target: 6 task clusters x 2 repetitions x 27 conditions = 324 sequence outcomes; prefixes intentionally shared
inputs: Binary endpoint and paired differences in [-1,1]
Two repetitions do not make 12 independent task samples
sampling.dependence_structure: Task clusters and shared producer stages retained in paired resampling
sampling.multiplicity: One declared primary contrast; all other comparisons exploratory
sampling.attrition_or_loss: Failure counted in endpoint denominator; unknown charged usage remains missing, never zero
sampling.result: A worst-case normal paired-difference half-width is approximately 1.96/sqrt(6)=0.80; this is too imprecise for a general 10 percentage-point claim. The study is a feasibility/regression pilot.
sampling.sensitivity_analysis: At 12/24/48 independent tasks, the same conservative approximation gives half-widths 0.57/0.40/0.28. Degenerate bootstrap intervals at all-success are explicitly uninformative about unseen failures. A pre-execution simulation (relay-precision-simulation.json, seed20260924, 1000 datasets per scenario) found nominal95% percentile coverage of0.738–0.889 with six task clusters under three specified paired-difference distributions and perfectly correlated repetitions. Monte Carlo standard errors are retained. These intervals are descriptive and must not be advertised as calibrated95% population coverage.
sampling.stopping_implications: Fixed 324 endpoints unless declared cost or access stop; preserve every scheduled missing endpoint and explain coverage

analysis.preprocessing_lock: Exact status equality. No exclusions based on model performance. Report unknown provider usage as unknown.
analysis.exclusion_lock: Only preflight connectivity probes excluded from task accuracy, with separate cost ledger

models.model_or_procedure: Paired finite-task means and 2000 percentile task-cluster bootstrap draws
assumptions: Task clusters are the resampling units; no random task-population claim
outputs: Per-condition accuracy, unjustified positives, cost, tokens and latency

contrasts: Secondary: reversed small/full, homogeneous chains, three-stage chains, reasoning tiers and tool placement
Transcript/evidence and evidence/none comparisons exploratory; none is a shared-input invariant
analysis.uncertainty: Whole tasks resampled with both repetitions and shared prefix relations intact; six clusters supply coarse descriptive intervals
analysis.multiplicity: No confirmatory p values or superiority claims. All searched pairwise contrasts retained and labelled exploratory.
analysis.missing_data: Incomplete final answers fail task resolution. Partial/unknown billing remains null. Do not drop failed trials.
analysis.stopping_rule: 324 scheduled sequences; $12 known campaign model-cost threshold, $0.20/stage and 180 seconds/stage, max10 requests and120000 tokens. Post-response thresholds may overshoot. Unknown billing halts further model calls. Continuation 1.0.8 runs the already declared five missing blocks in fresh serial cohorts. Each phase must satisfy the cumulative planning check in scripts/run_relay_completion.py; any new unknown usage stops both phases. Historical unknown usage is retained with a $4.50 planning allowance, not reported as a known charge.
